You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test (testMath274) constructs a symmetric matrix that is not positive definite and expects CholeskyDecompositionImpl to throw NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException. However, the constructor does not throw, causing the test to fail.

What the code does:
- CholeskyDecompositionImpl(RealMatrix, double, double) first performs pre-checks on the input matrix:
  - Non-square check (lines 99–102).
  - Symmetry check with a relative threshold and zeroing the lower part (lines 109–129).
  - A diagonal positivity check, but only on the original, untransformed diagonal entries (line 114).
- It then performs the in-place Cholesky transformation (lines 131–149):
  - For each i, it takes the square root of ltI[i] (line 138), computes its inverse (line 139), scales row i (line 142), and updates the trailing submatrix (lines 143–146).

Where the bug is:
- Positive definiteness for Cholesky decomposition must be validated on the updated pivot (the current diagonal element after all previous Schur complement updates), not just on the original diagonal.
- The code only checks the original diagonal entries before any transformation (line 114) and never re-checks the pivot inside the main loop before taking the square root (line 138).
- For an indefinite symmetric matrix, a pivot can become non-positive after the updates from previous steps. In that case, Math.sqrt(ltI[i]) (line 138) will yield NaN for ltI[i] < 0, and the algorithm will propagate NaNs without throwing any exception. Since there is no subsequent check, the constructor completes without throwing NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException.

How it causes the observed failure:
- The test matrix is symmetric (passes the symmetry check) but not positive definite. During factorization, one of the updated diagonal entries becomes non-positive.
- Because there is no check before the sqrt at line 138, the code computes sqrt on a non-positive value, producing NaN and continuing silently.
- No NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException is thrown, so the test that expects this exception fails.

Key code locations:
- Pre-check of original diagonal only (insufficient): CholeskyDecompositionImpl(RealMatrix, double, double), line 114.
- Missing positivity check on updated pivot before sqrt: CholeskyDecompositionImpl(RealMatrix, double, double), around lines 136–141 (specifically before line 138).

Correct behavior:
- Insert a positivity check on the updated diagonal element just before taking the square root inside the main loop, e.g., if (ltI[i] <= absolutePositivityThreshold) throw new NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException(); This ensures that an indefinite matrix triggers the expected exception at the moment a non-positive pivot is encountered.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
